questions.prompt: Authoritative data:
choices: Come from official agencies, follow documented standards, and have metadata
Are always more current than asserted data
questions.explain: The Census Bureau and USGS publish authoritative data.

questions.prompt: Which is an example of asserted (volunteered) data?
questions.explain: OpenStreetMap is contributed by volunteers.

questions.prompt: Asserted data are always less accurate than authoritative data.
questions.explain: Where contributors are active, asserted data can be more current and even more accurate.

questions.prompt: Income, education, and poverty are examples of:
questions.explain: They describe economic and social conditions, mostly from the ACS.

questions.prompt: In public health, census counts often serve as:
choices: Denominators that turn counts into rates
questions.explain: For example, deaths per 100,000 residents.

questions.prompt: As census geography gets finer:
choices: Fewer variables are published, and estimates are less precise
questions.explain: A block has a handful of counts; a state has thousands of tables.

questions.prompt: The decennial census is required by:
questions.explain: Article I, Section 2.

questions.prompt: In what year was the first U.S. census taken?
questions.explain: The 2020 Census was the 24th.

questions.prompt: Which question is on the 2020 decennial census?
choices: Whether the home is owned or rented
questions.explain: Income, education, and commuting come from the ACS.

questions.prompt: The American Community Survey:
choices: Samples about 3.5 million addresses a year for social, economic, and housing data
questions.explain: Most socioeconomic variables come from the ACS.

questions.prompt: The Economic Census is taken:
choices: Every 5 years, in years ending in 2 and 7
questions.explain: It profiles businesses.

questions.prompt: Decennial census counts are used to:
choices: Divide the 435 House seats among the states
questions.explain: That is apportionment.

questions.prompt: In fiscal year 2021, census data guided the distribution of about how much federal money?
questions.explain: Through 353 federal programs.

questions.prompt: The Post-Enumeration Survey measures:
choices: How many people the census missed or counted twice
questions.explain: For 2020 it found undercounts of Hispanic and Black residents.

questions.prompt: Differential privacy in the 2020 Census:
choices: Adds calibrated noise so individuals can't be identified
questions.explain: Small-area counts can look odd as a result.

questions.prompt: Individual census records are released after how many years?
questions.explain: The 1950 records were released in 2022.

questions.prompt: Put these census geographies in order, from largest to smallest.
questions.explain: Each level nests inside the one above.

questions.prompt: Which is off the census spine?
questions.explain: ZCTAs are built from blocks but cross tract boundaries.

questions.prompt: Every block group lies completely inside one census tract.
questions.explain: Spine levels nest completely.

questions.prompt: You can get a ZCTA's population by adding up whole census tracts.
questions.explain: ZCTAs are off the spine and cross tract boundaries.

questions.prompt: A ZCTA never matches a ZIP Code exactly because:
choices: ZIP Codes are mail routes, not areas
questions.explain: ZCTAs approximate them with blocks.

questions.prompt: A census tract typically has:
questions.explain: Tracts are the usual unit for neighborhood studies.

questions.prompt: A block group typically has:
questions.explain: They are clusters of blocks within a tract.

questions.prompt: What is the smallest geography with ACS estimates?
questions.explain: Blocks get decennial counts only.

questions.prompt: Census blocks are bounded by:
choices: Streets, streams, rail lines, and other visible features
questions.explain: There were more than 8 million blocks in 2020.

questions.prompt: How many digits are in a county GEOID?
questions.explain: 2 for the state + 3 for the county.

questions.prompt: How many digits are in a block group GEOID?
questions.explain: 11 for the tract + 1 for the block group.

questions.prompt: How many digits are in a block GEOID?
questions.explain: 11 for the tract + 4 for the block.

questions.prompt: The county GEOID 37135 is made of:
questions.explain: State FIPS + county FIPS.

questions.prompt: In a block GEOID, the block group is:
choices: The first digit of the four-digit block number
A separate code at the end
questions.explain: Block 1003 is in block group 1.

questions.prompt: ACS 1-year estimates are published only for areas with at least:
questions.explain: No tract or block group has 1-year estimates.

questions.prompt: ACS 5-year estimates are:
choices: Available down to block groups and the most reliable, but the least current
questions.explain: They pool 60 months of data.

questions.prompt: You need median rent for every tract in Wake County. Use:
questions.explain: Tracts have only 5-year estimates, and rent isn't on the decennial census.

questions.prompt: You need the number of children under 5 in each block. Use:
questions.explain: Blocks get decennial counts only, and age is on the decennial form.

questions.prompt: It is fine to compare an ACS 1-year estimate with an ACS 5-year estimate.
questions.explain: Compare like with like.

questions.prompt: A margin of error tells you:
choices: The likely range of sampling error around an estimate
questions.explain: Every ACS estimate has one.

questions.prompt: Census Bureau margins of error use what confidence level?
questions.explain: About 90 of 100 repeated samples would give a range containing the true value.

questions.prompt: A poll finds 55% prefer Coffee A, with a margin of error of ±3 points. The true share is likely:
Two tracts have margins of error of 300 and 400 people. What is the margin of error of their sum?
An estimate of 10,000 has a margin of error of 1,645. What is its coefficient of variation, in percent?
A common rule of thumb treats an ACS estimate as unreliable when its CV is over:
questions.explain: Under 12% reliable; 12–40% use with caution.

questions.prompt: Many block-group estimates have huge margins of error. A good fix is to:
choices: Use larger areas, such as tracts, or broader categories
questions.explain: Combining reduces the relative error.

questions.prompt: Which source offers census tables back to 1790 with matching boundaries?
questions.explain: NHGIS also offers tables on consistent boundaries over time.

questions.prompt: TIGER/Line shapefiles provide:
choices: Official boundaries for census geographies, with GEOIDs
questions.explain: Join census tables to them on the GEOID.

questions.prompt: In the ArcGIS Pro tutorial, why add a Long field, fips5, to the county layer?
choices: So both key fields have the same data type
To remove leading zeros from the map
questions.explain: The CSV's ID was read as a number, and a CSV is read-only, so the layer gets a matching numeric field.

questions.prompt: In ArcGIS Pro's Add Join, Validate Join tells you:
choices: How many records match before you run the join
questions.explain: For North Carolina's counties, all 100 should match.
